c.tagline: China's busiest land port, where Russian onion domes, Mongolian grasslands, and a 30-meter Matryoshka doll collide

card: Credit cards are rarely accepted outside international-standard hotels; WeChat Pay and Alipay dominate — set up mobile payment before arrival. Russian rubles are informally accepted in some border-trade shops but yuan is standard.

taxi.color: mixed liveries, mostly red and white sedans
taxi.fareNote: Meters are standard in town; trips to Hulun Lake or the border-crossing tourist area are usually flat-rate — agree the price upfront

emergency.note: Fire is 119. English support is minimal — Russian is more commonly understood than English due to cross-border trade.

religion: small Russian Orthodox and Christian minority
walk: Central Manzhouli's main boulevards (Erdaojie area) are walkable and lined with distinctive Russian-influenced architecture; Hulun Lake and the border crossing require a taxi, Didi, or tour bus.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers; a well-policed border-trade city with low crime
safety.crime: Minimal — standard caution around border-market bargaining and currency exchange is enough

hood_landmark.Central Manzhouli (Erdaojie): Matryoshka Square and the Russian-style boulevard architecture
hood_landmark.Hulun Lake (Dalai Nur) Area: Hulun Lake's grassland shoreline and birdwatching spots
hood_landmark.Xingfu (Happiness) District: Local residential streets and everyday markets

hood_desc: The city's showpiece core, where candy-colored Russian-revival buildings, the giant Matryoshka doll landmarks, and nightly illuminated light shows draw domestic tourists after dark.
The working border-crossing zone where Chinese and Russian traders exchange goods, with markets selling Russian chocolate, vodka, and souvenirs alongside customs facilities.
A grassland lake area about 45 minutes from downtown, popular for birdwatching, horseback riding, and Mongolian-style yurt stays in summer.
The historic railway quarter built during the Russian-administered Chinese Eastern Railway era, with the city's oldest surviving station architecture.
A quieter residential district away from the tourist core, with everyday shops and local eateries for a look at ordinary Manzhouli life.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as everywhere in China.

transit.sys: City buses cover the compact downtown core
transit.note: Manzhouli's core is small and walkable; buses and Didi cover Hulun Lake and the border zone

transport.air: Manzhouli Xijiao International Airport (NZH), ~12 km from downtown, with domestic flights to Beijing, Hohhot, Harbin and other cities
transport.train: Manzhouli railway station, a historic stop on the Chinese Eastern Railway, connects to Harbin, Beijing, and cross-border toward Zabaykalsk, Russia
transport.bus: Long-distance buses and cross-border coaches connect Manzhouli to Hailar and, via the border crossing, to Zabaykalsk, Russia
transport.ferry: None — Manzhouli is a landlocked border city with no passenger ferry service
transport.car: Self-driving or a hired car is useful for reaching Hulun Lake and the surrounding grasslands; Highway 301 links Manzhouli to Hailar and the wider Hulunbuir region

airport.name: Manzhouli Xijiao International Airport
airport.transport: Airport shuttle bus to the city center; taxi/Didi also available

net.m: Good 4G in downtown Manzhouli; weaker out on the Hulun Lake grasslands
net.w: Free wifi common in hotels and cafes downtown
net.ops: China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom
net.gb: ~$3-5 per GB on a prepaid tourist SIM
net.fwn: The Great Firewall blocks Google, WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook — install a VPN before arrival
net.ap: Buy a SIM or eSIM in Beijing or Harbin before traveling to Manzhouli; local stock is limited

tip.s: Not expected — tipping isn't part of Chinese service culture
tip.r: No tipping at restaurants; rarely a service charge outside upscale hotel restaurants
